_about: SEC Newgate 'Mood of the Nation' one-off and rotating survey questions that do NOT channel into the auspol-tracker data model (voting intention/leader trackers are not SEC Newgate products; national direction IS channelled via polls.json direction[] and is excluded, as are the committed mood/priority pipelines). Compiled by reading the seven committed report text dumps in .build/secnewgate-src/ (Jul 2025 through Sep 2026, waves 21-27); waves before 21 are unaudited and stay out.
_readme: Two-store convention: a question gets ONE id; every wave that asked it files a dated reading under it (identical ids across waves are the series, e.g. immigration-level in waves 24/26/27). Entry metadata (waveDate/sample/published/url/methodUrl) comes from the matching polls.json direction[] row for the wave. Every figure in every table was token-verified present in the report text dump at filing time; notes cite value orders inline. Rendering contract (read before editing): tables[0] is always width-1 (one value per entity) so the /ad-hocs/ headline strip renders it as labelled bars; multi-value tables carry 'columns' parallel to 'values'; gen-data.mjs maps columns->headers and entities->rows like the News24 store. Width-1 tables may omit 'columns'. width-1 headline tables whose rows were derived from a wider printed row mark the derivation in their title. trump-sentiment (filed 2026-10-17 at user request for the cross-house Trump series): the standing sentiment module (old N22 renumbered N24 then N30) printed as a chart strip only in each report; all seven waves' totals and scale rows are printed in the reports' 'Level of positivity or negativity' trend strips and token-verified. Total columns are the report's own printed TOTAL POSITIVE/NEGATIVE (July 2025's printed totals 15/70 are rounded before its scale rows). No demographic table is printed for this module; highlights quoted in notes come from each report's section prose.

entries.question: Which do you think should be the top 3 priorities for the Federal Government over the next 3 years?
entries.notes: Participants were given a list of 8 options. Investment in the health system (61%) and affordable housing (59%) lead, with tax reform third (43%); disaster preparedness (18%) and apprenticeships (16%) rank last. Among 18–34s affordable housing tops the list at 72% (48% of 65+), while 37% of 65+ select national defence vs 11% of 18–34s; men pick tax reform 48% vs women 39%. Values are % selected as top 3 priority.

entries.question: What impact do you think the transition to renewable energy will have on electricity bills over the following time periods?
entries.notes: 47% think the renewables transition will put upward pressure on electricity bills over the next 1-4 years (36% downward pressure or no impact), easing to 38% over 5-9 years and 31% over 10-20 years (45% downward or none). entries.question: Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom have formed a long-term security partnership known as AUKUS. The agreement aims to strengthen defence and security cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region, including helping Australia acquire nuclear-powered submarines and access advanced defence technologies. Do you support or oppose Australia's involvement in the AUKUS partnership?
entries.notes: 59% support Australia's AUKUS involvement (one in four, 25%, strongly), 23% neutral, 17% opposed. The partisan gap is 39 points: Coalition 74% vs Greens 35% support, and Greens are 34% opposed vs 8% of Coalition supporters; 65+ at 71% support vs 52% of 18-34s.

entries.question: How do you rate the current relationship between Australia and the following countries?
entries.notes: New Zealand (88% good+) and the United Kingdom (80%) rate best; China (34%) and Russia (10%) worst. The US is the big mover, up to 53% good+ from 38% in April 2025, while most others slipped a few points (UK 85→80, Canada 77→71, Germany 63→59, France 62→58).

entries.question: Overall, how confident are you in the ability of governments to respond and assist if a natural disaster (such as a hail storm, cyclone, flood or bushfire) was to occur in your local area?
entries.notes: 71% are confident governments would respond to a local natural disaster, but only 12% are 'very' confident (59% somewhat); 29% not confident. 65+ (76%) and WA (76%) are the most confident, 35-49s the least (66%), and regional Australia is less confident than metro (32% vs 28% not confident).

Support climbs with age (65+ and 50-64 both 54% vs 44% of 35-49s); Greens are the least supportive partisan group at 37% vs Coalition 54% and Labor 52%.

entries.question: Do you support or oppose large scale protests occurring in each of the following places, as a way to express political or social views?

entries.question: In the Federal Budget handed down in May, the Federal Government announced changes to the capital gains tax (CGT) discount on assets (such as investment properties, shares, or small business assets) held for more than a year. The current rule – where only 50% of any profit is taxed – will be replaced. Under the new system, when an asset is sold, the profit will first be reduced to account for inflation over the time it was held, and the remaining gain will then be taxed, with a minimum tax rate of 30%.
